newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Offered down depite firmer West.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Offered down depite firmer West.

text.p: Singapore gasoline prices fell on Thursday despite overnight gains in the West, traders said.

The NYMEX August gasoline contract to its highest level on Wednesday since January as tightening supply amid strong demand trigered fresh buying interest. The contract surged by 3.43 cents per gallon to 69.90. It added a further 0.60 to 70.50 on ACCESS trade.

But on the Singapore fob market, a European major and Dutch trader lowered their respectively offers of August 92-octane and 95-octane to $22.60 and $23.59 per barrel from $22.80 and $23.80 on Wednesday.
"In a normal perfect market, prices should be supported by the strength in the West," said one trader. "But the Singapore market is quite a different animal."
But the firm Western markets have spurred a few enquires for arbitrage cargoes to the U.S. West Coast.
"The arbitrage is open but the strict quality is the set back," said a seller.

Traders assessed the market balanced with supplies of high-octane tight with reduced reformer output and demand from the Philippines and Malaysia while low octane is well supplied with cargoes available from China in August.

Offers into Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp's closed tender for 100,000 barrels of 95 or 97-octane unleaded reformate for delivery August 10-20, were heard around $5 over Singapore naphtha spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The tender closed on July 28 but results have yet to be announced.
Naphtha held steady despite crude gains as the market was spooked by talks of an emergency shutdown of a South Korean refiner's 600,000 tonnes per year ethylene plant.
August swaps were last quoted at $21.80/$22.00, marginally lower than Wednesday's $21.95/$22.05.
